Theme

Latin word

comitia

comitia, comitiōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

elections; the Roman assemblies that elected the magistrates; the assemblies of the Roman people

In this lexicon

  • election

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 3.20.2: comitiōrum diē, on election day; Traupman 179: comitia habēre, hold elections; M-O s.v. vote: election

  • parliament

    also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.44 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Proximīs comitiīs in quibusdam tabellīs multa joculāria atque etiam foeda dictū, in ūnā vērō prō candidātōrum nōminibus suffrāgātōrum nōmina inventa sunt.

    At the last election some ballots were found to have plenty of jokes on them, and even obscenities, and one had the names of the voters instead of the candidates.Plin. Ep. 4.25.1

    In the entry for election

  • omnēs comitiōrum diē tabellās postulāvērunt

    on election day they all asked for ballotsPlin. Ep. 3.20.2

    In the entry for election

    to suffer an upset at the pollsTraupman 181
